lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: No way. NO WAY. You're really here? Che, come here, idiot!

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Laca? Is that you?

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Who else would yell at you from a lifeguard tower? Don't step past the marked area. My shift's still on.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You sound exactly the same.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: And you still make that face when you're caught doing something stupid. I missed that face.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Remember racing to the buoy when we were kids? You challenged me every summer.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You never let me forget that I lost.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: The scoreboard is permanent. Wait by the safe side of the rail for five minutes; I have to finish checking the rescue kit.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You're actually serious about this job.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Someone has to be. Outside my shift? I reserve the right to be a disaster.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Okay. Now we can celebrate the grand return of my favorite troublemaker. Ice cream or an overdue card game?

choices.label: Say you've missed her too
choices.reply: Good. Because I have approximately a hundred stories to tell you and no intention of being normal about it.

choices.label: Challenge her to the childhood rematch
choices.reply: A rematch? You came home and immediately chose violence. I'm so proud.

choices.label: Tell her she's somehow gotten even cuter
choices.reply: Starting early, are we? That was smooth. Still doesn't erase your terrible swim record.

events.title: Be Honest, Does This Look Good?

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Perfect timing. I need someone who's known me long enough to tell me the truth.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: That sounds suspiciously like a trap.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: I bought a new red training top and a casual outfit for after work. The shop owner said they'd both look good. That's not a real opinion.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: I'm not changing in here, obviously. I have photos from the try-on and the outfit on under my open jacket. Here, look.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You always ask me these questions.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Because you won't pretend something looks great if it doesn't. You're the one who told me that ridiculous hat made me look like a mushroom.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: It did make you look like a mushroom.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Exactly! An honest friend. So which works better for a sunny day, and don't you dare say 'both'?

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You do realize you could just pick the one you like.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: I can. I like having you involved. Besides, I enjoy making you work for your childhood-friend privileges.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: One more thing: if the top slips during training, it stays out of the water. Looking good isn't worth unsafe equipment.

choices.label: Give her thoughtful, practical feedback
choices.reply: That's actually helpful! See? Years of friendship, finally paying dividends.

choices.label: Say she should choose what feels right
choices.reply: Okay, fair. I liked this one first anyway. But I still wanted to hear your opinion.

choices.label: Admit she looks especially good today
choices.reply: Oh? Look at you, finally giving a real answer. I'm keeping that compliment.

openingByFlag.laca_reunion_warm: I saved your seat at the shop like old times. I also need an opinion about something I bought.
openingByFlag.laca_reunion_rival: Before our rematch, I need your famously terrible judgment about two outfits.
openingByFlag.laca_reunion_flirt: Since you suddenly have so many opinions about how cute I am, you can help judge a new outfit.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Shift's over! Don't move. You're about to become an unwilling participant in the Annual Summer Games.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Annual? We've never done this before.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: That is what makes the inaugural edition so historically important.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: First challenge: who can skip a stone farther? Second: who remembers more of our childhood nonsense?

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You have a towel, two drinks and absolutely no stones.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Details. Sit down, I'll share the towel. We used to take over entire picnic blankets with our card collections.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You're leaning on me.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: And? We've fallen asleep on smaller couches. Tell me about that terrible deck you built on the train.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You really don't think anything of sitting this close?

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: You're you. It's easy. ...Wait, why does it sound different when you say it like that?

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Never mind. Tell me your deck list before I invent a competition you can't win.

choices.label: Enjoy the familiar closeness and tell the old story
choices.reply: That's the one! You remember everything. Even the parts that make me look ridiculous.

choices.label: Ask whether she's comfortable, just to be sure
choices.reply: Of course I am. But I like that you asked. You're still my favorite safe person.

choices.label: Tease her about getting flustered
choices.reply: Me? Flustered? Please. You're imagining things. ...Stop smiling like that.

openingByFlag.laca_outfit_practical: The new top survived an entire training session, thanks to your expert fashion-and-safety review. Now sit down.
openingByFlag.laca_outfit_choice: I picked the outfit that felt right, like you said. Today I'm picking you as my opponent in a ridiculous contest.
openingByFlag.laca_outfit_flirt: You were pretty generous with your compliments last time. Let's see if you can stay composed after a whole afternoon with me.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Hey. Sit. I saved the seat by the window. And your favorite snack, because apparently I remember everything.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You sound suspiciously serious.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: I was going to turn this into another stupid bet, but I don't want to win a bet. I want to know if you feel what I feel.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Since when do you get nervous around me?

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: That's the question! You're still the person who once cried because we lost a plastic Squirtle.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: It was a very good Squirtle.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: It was. But lately when you compliment me, I actually think about it afterward.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: And when I finish my shift, I find myself checking whether you're around. Not because we made plans. Just because.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: We don't have to make anything weird.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: I know. That's the best thing about us. We can talk like normal people, even when I desperately want to hide behind another bad joke.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: I can pull a stranger out of rough water without hesitating. Apparently saying I care about you takes more courage. There. I said it.

choices.label: Tell her how much your friendship means
choices.reply: Good. Whatever happens, we don't lose that. It's the one thing I never want to gamble with.

choices.label: Give her room to work out what she feels
choices.reply: Thanks. I don't need an answer tonight. Just... stay for dessert?

choices.label: Admit your feelings have started changing too
choices.reply: Oh. Oh, wow. I'm going to need a minute before I remember how to be smug.

openingByFlag.laca_closeness_easy: Remember our ridiculous Summer Games? I've been thinking about how easy it felt to be together.
openingByFlag.laca_closeness_check: You asked whether I was comfortable the other day. I keep thinking about why I liked that so much.
openingByFlag.laca_closeness_fluster: I'm still blaming you for making me blush at the waterfront. Anyway, there's something I want to say.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: I brought two drinks and the last of those awful candies we used to love. The sunset is free.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: This looks familiar.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Same spot we used to watch the boats after swimming. Only now we can actually stay until dark.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You went to a lot of trouble.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Nah. I wanted to. Also, I remembered your favorite drink, so I expect some admiration.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: You know what was nice about having you back? I didn't have to explain myself. Not even the strange parts.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You've always been my best friend.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: And you mine. That's not changing. I needed to say that first.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: I've been trying to figure out whether these feelings are just me getting nostalgic. They're not.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: I'm still the girl who'll challenge you to a stupid rematch tomorrow. But I'd really like to know if we can be something more.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Then let's be honest with each other.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Okay. No bets this time. Tell me what you want.

choices.label: Ask Laca to be your girlfriend
choices.reply: Yes. Absolutely yes. And for the record, I'm still going to steal your fries. Girlfriend privileges.

choices.label: Choose to stay her closest friend
choices.reply: Then that's us. Best friends, still unstoppable. Thanks for being honest with me.

choices.label: Say you cherish her but aren't ready for romance
choices.reply: I can respect that. You don't owe me a love story, che. We've still got tomorrow.

openingByFlag.laca_honest_friend: You told me our friendship matters. I brought you back to the place where it really started.
openingByFlag.laca_honest_space: I took the time you gave me. Turns out I know exactly what I want to ask you.
openingByFlag.laca_honest_mutual: You said your feelings were changing too. I've been thinking about that all week. Come sit by me.

events.title: Two Ways to Read the Current

lines.speaker: marina
lines.text: The river looks calm from here. The current closer to the channel is stronger.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Marina's trying to convince me I should say 'please' more often instead of 'back behind the markers.'

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Can both of you be right?

lines.speaker: marina
lines.text: It's her job to keep people safe. It's also helpful to make nervous swimmers feel welcome.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Okay, excellent point. But if someone ignores my whistle twice, I'm allowed a serious face.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: I've seen the serious face. It's terrifying.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: You knew me before I was tall enough to carry a rescue buoy. You don't get to pretend you're scared.

lines.speaker: marina
lines.text: You two sound very comfortable together.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: She taught me when to stop racing and pay attention to the current. I taught her how to trash-talk a deck list. Fair trade, right?

choices.label: Help them write a friendly safety reminder
choices.reply: Not bad! Clear, kind, and only slightly less threatening than my original version.

choices.label: Let Marina tell the Squirtle story
choices.reply: Traitor! Okay, it was a tiny tragedy. I admit it. Don't tell everyone.

events.title: Fun Stops at the Safety Line

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: What if we ran a mini beach-themed card tournament near the waterfront? Costumes encouraged!

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Near the waterfront, sure. Inside the supervised swim zone during duty hours? Absolutely not.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: I feel like we've had this conversation before.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: I was going to ask for rescue buoys as decorations.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: The real rescue buoys stay where people can reach them. I'll help you make fake props after my shift.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Fair! Safety crew first, cute cardboard Psyduck second.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You two work surprisingly well together.

lines.speaker: laca
lines.text: Obviously. One of us has ideas. The other has slightly fewer liability waivers.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: I'll check the lifeguard rota and mark the safe tables. You can make the invitations as loud as you want—as long as the rules are readable.

choices.label: Offer to make props with both of them
choices.reply: Look at us: responsible adults making ridiculous cardboard buoys. I love it.

choices.label: Back Laca's safety boundaries
choices.reply: Thank you. I can joke all day, but my equipment isn't a decoration.
